title: Name the mysteries too sublime for Scripture — image-cult is not greater than the Trinity
source_text: XXXIV. Deinde nobis edant Pontificii quaenam sint illa mysteria, quorum dignitas & majestas tanta est, ut non debuerint in sacris Scripturis explicari. Nam certe mysterium de mundi creatione, & ejus interitu, de resurrectione corporum, de Filii Dei incarnatione, de duabus in Christo naturis, de tribus personis in una divina essentia, & plura ejusmodi, in Scripturis exposita sunt. An vero Pontificii proferre possunt mysteria his augustiora atque sublimiora? Et num dogma de cultu imaginum, de invocatione Sanctorum, & de successione Papae in locum Petri Apostoli, sunt aliquid excellius, & majori veneratione dignum, quam personarum trinitas in Deo, generis humani redemptio per mortem Dei incarnati pro nobis, ut haec quidem scribi potuerint, illa vero non decuerint scribi? Denique quis est ille furor existimare, non fuisse de dignitate traditionum, ut ab Apostolis scriberentur, istam vero illarum dignitatem non violari, cum centies a gregariis Doctoribus scriptis mandantur, atque omnibus inculcantur.
pass_a_gloss: Next let the Pontificii tell us what those mysteries are, whose dignity and majesty is so great that they ought not to have been explained in the sacred Scriptures. For certainly the mystery of the creation of the world, and of its destruction, of the resurrection of bodies, of the incarnation of the Son of God, of the two natures in Christ, of the three persons in one divine essence, and more of that kind, are set out in the Scriptures. But can the Pontificii bring forward mysteries more august and more sublime than these? And are the dogma of the cult of images, of the invocation of the Saints, and of the succession of the Pope into the place of the Apostle Peter, something more excellent, and worthy of greater veneration, than the trinity of persons in God, the redemption of the human race through the death of God incarnate for us, so that these indeed could be written, but those ought not to have been written? Finally what madness is that — to judge that it was not of the dignity of the traditions that they be written by the Apostles, yet that their dignity is not violated when a hundred times they are committed to writing by ordinary Doctors and drilled into everyone.
pass_b_english: Challenge: name the mysteries too sublime for Scripture.
Creation, judgment, resurrection, incarnation, two natures, Trinity — already written.
Image-cult, saint-invocation, papal succession are not higher than Trinity and the cross.
Madness: Apostolic writing would degrade tradition, yet ordinary doctors print it daily.
